title: Wake Up
summary: You doze off on the train home and wake somewhere wrong: a silent car of passengers hidden behind newspapers, a phone stuck at 2:14, black windows, stops you've never heard of. An old woman is horrified to see you; she doesn't know where you are either. She introduces herself as June, talks with you, notices your stop isn't on the map, and gives you nine handwritten rules. The conductor punches tickets; a man in a red tracksuit nearly talks back and June saves him. June's own ticket is punched like lace. Then the man in red mocks the passengers, they copy him, he won't freeze, the lights go out, and he's gone. On the front page of a newspaper where he stood is a man in a red tracksuit.

lines.spoken: You finally catch the train home after a long day. All you want is your bed.
lines.caption: after a **long day**

lines.spoken: The second you sit down, the fatigue hits. A small nap couldn't hurt.
lines.caption: a small **nap**

lines.spoken: If only you knew how wrong you'd be.
lines.caption: how **wrong** you'd be

lines.spoken: You wake up to silence. Just the clack of the tracks.
lines.caption: the **clack** of the tracks

lines.spoken: Every passenger hides behind a newspaper. Nobody moves.
lines.caption: **nobody moves**

lines.spoken: Two fourteen in the morning. No signal.
lines.caption: **2:14**. **no signal**

lines.spoken: The route map lists stops you've never heard of.
lines.caption: stops you've **never heard of**

lines.spoken: Across the aisle, an old woman knits a scarf so long it trails across the floor.
lines.caption: an **old woman** knits

lines.spoken: She's the only one not reading. She's watching you.
lines.caption: she's **watching** you

lines.spoken: When your eyes meet, her face falls.
lines.caption: her **face falls**

lines.spoken: "Oh no," she whispers. "Not another one."
lines.caption: **not another one**

lines.spoken: "Where are we?" you ask.
lines.caption: **where** are we

lines.spoken: "I'm not sure, sweetheart. I wish I knew."
lines.caption: **I'm not sure**

lines.spoken: She sits down beside you. "I'm June. Fell asleep too?"
lines.caption: **I'm June**

lines.spoken: You nod. "Long day." "They always are," June says.
lines.caption: they **always** are

lines.spoken: "Where were you headed?" she asks. "Elm Street."
lines.caption: **Elm Street**

lines.spoken: June glances at the map. Elm Street isn't on it.
lines.caption: **isn't on it**

lines.spoken: "Okay," June says quietly. "Then listen to me carefully."
lines.caption: **listen** to me

lines.spoken: She presses a folded sheet into your hands. "Do exactly what it says."
lines.caption: do **exactly** what it says

lines.spoken: Rule one. Do not make eye contact with the other passengers.
lines.caption: do not make **eye contact**

lines.spoken: Rule two. When the conductor asks for your ticket, smile. Do not speak.
lines.caption: **smile**. do not **speak**

lines.spoken: Rule three. If the lights go out, keep your eyes closed until the doors chime.
lines.caption: keep your **eyes closed**

lines.spoken: Rule four. Never go into the last car.
lines.caption: never the **last car**

lines.spoken: Rule five. If someone calls your name, it isn't them.
lines.caption: it **isn't them**

lines.spoken: Rule six. Your stop is the one that shows your name. Get off, no matter what's on the platform.
lines.caption: the one that shows your **name**

lines.spoken: Rule seven. Do not fall asleep again.
lines.caption: do not fall **asleep again**

lines.spoken: Rule eight. If your reflection blinks before you do, look away.
lines.caption: your **reflection** blinks

lines.spoken: Rule nine. If the passengers start copying you, freeze.
lines.caption: **freeze**

lines.spoken: Then, from the end of the car: click. Click.
lines.caption: **click**. **click**.

lines.spoken: A tall conductor comes down the aisle, punching tickets. His cap hides his eyes. Not his smile.
lines.caption: not his **smile**

lines.spoken: A man in a red tracksuit films him. "Bro, is this a prank show?"
lines.caption: a **red tracksuit**

lines.spoken: "Ticket, please." The man starts to argue. June kicks his shoe, hard.
lines.caption: June **kicks** his shoe

lines.spoken: He blinks, then grins. Click. The conductor moves on.
lines.caption: he **grins**

lines.spoken: Then he's at your seat. "Ticket, please."
lines.caption: **ticket**, please

lines.spoken: In your pocket is a ticket you never bought. You smile. Click.
lines.caption: you **smile**. **click**.

lines.spoken: June stares at the hole, then holds up her own ticket. It's punched so many times it looks like lace.
lines.caption: it looks like **lace**

lines.spoken: "One hole," she whispers, "for every stop you miss."
lines.caption: every **stop** you miss

lines.spoken: "Watch this," the man in red laughs, and waves at the passengers.
lines.caption: "**watch this**"

lines.spoken: Every newspaper drops. Every hand in the car waves back.
lines.caption: every hand **waves back**

lines.spoken: "Freeze," June hisses. You go still. He doesn't.
lines.caption: you go **still**. he **doesn't**.

lines.spoken: He stands and bows. They all stand and bow. He laughs. They laugh, silently.
lines.caption: they **laugh**, silently

lines.spoken: Then every passenger takes one step toward him.
lines.caption: one **step** toward him

lines.spoken: The lights go out.
lines.caption: the lights **go out**

lines.spoken: When the lights flicker on, his seat is empty.
lines.caption: his seat is **empty**

lines.spoken: On the floor lies a newspaper. Front page: a man in a red tracksuit.
lines.caption: a man in a **red tracksuit**

shots.frame: your seat, the ordinary train home

continuity_out: Night 1, still 2:14 AM. June sits beside you; you've told her your stop is Elm Street, which isn't on the map. You hold the nine rules (neat small handwriting you haven't recognised yet) and a ticket with one hole. June's ticket is punched hundreds of times. The man in the red tracksuit is gone: he wouldn't freeze when the passengers copied him; after the lights went out his seat was empty and a newspaper on the floor showed him on the front page. The conductor moved on toward the last car.
